The 2nd & 1 pass rate evolves over time as a function of strategic adaptation, while run/pass rates after 1st & 10 outcomes reflect immediate tactical responses. These operators form a Markov chain in play-state space, where each transition is governed by empirical frequency distributions. The failure mode occurs when these distributions are not stationary or when external factors (e.g., injuries, weather) alter baseline behavior without updating the model. Dualities emerge in the symmetry of pass/run decisions under similar down-distance conditions, suggesting a potential symmetry-breaking mechanism in strategic evolution.
